audit_2026_11_08: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-11-08) — post-WAVE1 order worked in the 2026-11-08 candidate audits: Mecklenburg County NC was re-audited and its collapse stands (SKIP); San Diego CA, Pinellas County FL, and Sacramento CA surfaced no engine-ready record-level feed (SKIP); Columbus OH passed. (1) Layer 'BuildingPermits' (City of Columbus 'Building Permits' FeatureServer, ArcGIS item owner ColumbusOhioGIS, public access): 689,367 rows all-time; item description: 'building permits issued by the City of Columbus Department of Building and Zoning Services. The period of record is 2010 to present.' Layer editingInfo.dataLastEditDate 2026-11-08T10:04:08Z (the morning of the audit). (2) VOLUME STABILITY measured by issued year: 2021 43,557 / 2022 41,508 / 2023 43,033 / 2024 41,147 / 2025 40,604 / 2026 YTD through Nov 6 38,493 — no collapse; months in the window run 2,666-4,427. Every row carries ISSUED_DT (0 null of 689,367): the layer is an issued-permits register; the window is ISSUED_DT >= 2025-11-08. (3) IDENTITY measured three ways on the window (two count queries + one full paged pull saved as the audit evidence): 43,861 rows = 43,861 distinct B1_ALT_ID = 43,861 distinct OBJECTID, 0 null ids — one row per permit, no collapsing. B1_PER_GROUP is 'Building' on 100% of window rows. Window statuses (PERMIT_STATUS): Permit Issued 23,767 / Final Inspection Approved 19,607 / Certificate of Occupancy Issued 262 / Expired Permit 225 — all post-issuance states. September 2026 cross-check figure: 4,041 permits; October 2026: 4,093; November 2026 to Nov 6: 1,035; latest issue date 2026-11-06. (4) VALUATION FAILED — counts-only (see field_map.valuation for the three defects). (5) Terms: the item's licenseInfo dedicates the data to the public domain under CC0 (Creative Commons Universal License) — the cleanest terms in the program. Audit evidence: ~/workspace/goals/permitsbycounty/hidden_files/expansion-2026-11-08/.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Columbus only. Columbus also extends into Delaware and Fairfield counties, and other Franklin County jurisdictions publish their permits separately and are not in this feed; totals here are City of Columbus totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one B1_ALT_ID in the City of Columbus's Building Permits layer. The layer's grain is one row per permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (ISSUED_DT >= 2025-11-08), measured 2026-11-08 on three consistent reads (two count queries + a full paged pull of the window): 43,861 rows = 43,861 distinct B1_ALT_ID = 43,861 distinct OBJECTID, 0 duplicates, 0 null permit numbers. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: SITE_ADDRESS, as published (present on 43,861 of 43,861 window permits; all-caps values title-cased, the Raleigh treatment). ZIP from B1_SITUS_ZIP (present on 43,848 of 43,861).
field_map.application_date: NULL — the layer publishes no application-date field (ISSUED_DT and LAST_STATUS_DT only), so application_date stays NULL by construction (the Philadelphia/Boston treatment). LAST_STATUS_DT is carried as the record's last-updated date (source_updated_date, epoch ms converted).
field_map.category: B1_PER_TYPE, the city's own building class: '1,2,3 Family' (31,082 window permits) and 'Multi Family' (4,615) = Residential (35,697); 'Commercial' (6,725) = Commercial; 'Graphics' (1,439 — the Sign permits) states no residential/commercial class and stays NULL.
field_map.contractor_rule: APPLICANT_BUS_NAME ONLY — the permit's published applicant business name of record (present on 40,077 of 43,861 window permits; 3,894 distinct; empty string carries as NULL). The source's literal 'PROPERTY OWNER' value (467 window permits — owner-permitted work, the Cincinnati 'OWNER' treatment) carries as NULL. The pull's column list never requests APPLICANT_FULL_NAME (person names, present on 23,226 rows) — excluded from pull_select by construction.
field_map.issue_date: ISSUED_DT (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when the city records an issue date; every row in the layer carries one.
field_map.permit_number: B1_ALT_ID (unique in the window, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.permit_type: B1_PER_CATEGORY, the city's own work family (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Roof/Siding/Windows/Doors family, Alteration, New Structure, Fire Alarm, Fire Suppression, ...).
field_map.project_description: Composed from the source's own labels, in this exact order: VALUE_DESC where present (16,751 window permits — the Census-style construction class the city states), else GENERAL_TYPE where present (42,411 window permits carry one), else B1_PER_CATEGORY. The layer publishes no free-text scope field, so no description is invented (the Cincinnati treatment).
field_map.status: PERMIT_STATUS, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Window statuses: Permit Issued 23,767 / Final Inspection Approved 19,607 / Certificate of Occupancy Issued 262 / Expired Permit 225 — every window record carries an issue date, so post-issuance states stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment). Status is taken from PERMIT_STATUS only (B1_APPL_STATUS carries 181 void/withdrawn rows that still show PERMIT_STATUS 'Permit Issued').
field_map.valuation: G3_VALUE_TTL FAILED validation on the full window (measured 2026-11-08) and is NOT published: valuation stays NULL in the DB and Franklin County runs counts-only (the Austin outcome). The raw field is carried into the vault in pull_select as reported, unpublished (the DeKalb treatment). Three independent defects: (1) ONE permit — a Perimeter Drainage Tile permit (PMEPI2613822, 4001 Olentangy River Rd, issued 2026-04-30) — states $6,143,270,689, which is 50.6% of the entire trailing-12-month raw sum ($12,145,275,048.55) on a drainage-tile permit — not a plausible per-permit value. (2) Project values are restated across sibling permits at the same address: $95,000,000 on both a New Structure and a Fire Alarm permit at 800 W North Broadway; $36,800,000 on an Alteration and a Fire Suppression permit at 40 W Long St; $13,400,000 at 240 Corrina Dr; $286,240,000 twice on two same-day New Structure permits at 6977 S High St. Same-address + same-value groups above $10k bound the restatement excess at $740,336,932 = 6.1% of the total, before counting the $6.14B outlier. (3) The field is structurally absent for the MEP trades (Mechanical valued on 6 of 11,077; Electrical 0 of 7,605; Plumbing 5 of 6,491) while present for structural categories — a fee-basis figure on part of the register, not a per-permit project value. Coverage in the bulk: null 3 / $0 28,278 (64.5%) / $1 3 / above $1 15,576. No honest county total exists; pages publish counts, trades, categories, and monthly volumes only, and the reason is stated on the Data Sources page.

history_range: ISSUED_DT 2010 onward in the source (689,367 rows, per the item description '2010 to present'); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: CC0 (Creative Commons Universal License — public domain dedication, named in the ArcGIS item's licenseInfo); attribution: City of Columbus, Ohio
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 2,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.
source_name: City of Columbus open data — Building Permits
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-08: the ArcGIS item record for 'Building Permits' (publisher: City of Columbus Department of Building and Zoning Services, owner ColumbusOhioGIS; access public) dedicates the data to the public domain under CC0 in its licenseInfo; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Columbus' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Daily in practice (the register is live — permits issued 2026-11-06 were in the feed at audit, and the layer was edited the morning of the audit); MEASURED 2026-11-08: layer dataLastEditDate 2026-11-08T10:04:08Z (same day as the audit, ~8h old) and newest ISSUED_DT 2026-11-06. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate under a 96h threshold (the Wake treatment).
watermark_field: ISSUED_DT + B1_ALT_ID — refresh re-pulls by the ISSUED_DT watermark and upserts.
